why:
Two Edits differing ONLY in how ApproximateLength is EXPRESSED are the same edit and must auto-match. Here the submitted side carries a float in minutes (41.5, as the XML adapter produces from PT41M30S) and the candidate carries ISO-8601 text (PT42M, as MirrorSource produces from the approximate_length column). Both display as 42 minutes.

`length_minutes` is HETEROGENEOUS by design, and comparing it raw is a bug: 41.5 == 'PT42M' is false. Every other consumer normalises through parse_minutes at the point of use, and render_record ceils to whole minutes for display -- so the gate must compare the value the REVIEWER SEES. Comparing raw demoted 115 of 264 Edit rows in the 2026-08-24 audit run whose displayed lengths were identical on both sides.

The principle, which generalises past this field: a reviewer must never be closed out by a difference the interface cannot show them.

Mutation-tested: reverting `_length_key` to a raw attribute read fails this fixture and no other.

SCOPE: pins the NORMALISATION, not the rule. It says nothing about whether a genuinely different length rejects.
